body: Wednesday, July 15 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed under new Chair Kevin Warsh remains on hold, described as "genuinely conflicted" on rates. June CPI slowed to 3.5%, which weakened the case for further hikes but is still well above target. The 10Y yield sits at 4.55 (+8 bps vs 4W ago) and the 2Y at 4.18 (prior close, +9 bps), so the curve is shifting up in parallel in a rising-yield environment — the market is pricing in higher-for-even-longer with a +40 bps slope that is positive but still flat by historical standards. Fiscal stance remains expansionary with no deficit discipline on the horizon.

New / Most Important: The soft June CPI print landed this week and was received positively — headlines called it "good news for Warsh and the stock market." However, Warsh's first rate decision at the July meeting looms as a defining moment. US-Iran escalation is simultaneously firming the dollar on safe-haven demand and threatening to re-accelerate energy-driven inflation, creating a genuine policy bind. 372 large US bankruptcies drew an "unexpected" credit market response — spreads apparently not blowing out despite stress, suggesting excess liquidity is still papering over micro credit deterioration. SpaceX shares fell below IPO price for the first time, a notable sentiment marker for the private-to-public tech liquidity narrative.

Playbook ✓: Breadth rotation from mega-cap tech into small caps is proceeding textbook — Russell 2000 (2970, ↑0.2%) outperforming Nasdaq 100 (29349, ↓3.9%), with the Russell/Nasdaq ratio up 4.2% in four weeks. VIX at 16.26 in complacency regime despite all the noise.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The CPI-to-yield disconnect is the structural story. CPI decelerated but 10Y yields are still climbing. This is NOT a classic "good inflation = lower yields" setup. The bond market is telling you something different — either term premium is being repriced higher on fiscal sustainability fears (issuance flood), or the Hormuz supply shock is being priced into forward breakevens even as backward-looking CPI cools. The credit market's blasé response to 372 large bankruptcies is equally anomalous — in prior cycles that volume of filings would trigger spread widening. Either CLO/private credit structures are absorbing losses quietly or we're seeing a dangerous complacency that ends abruptly. Watch the gap between bankruptcies and spreads — when it closes, it closes fast.

Macro Stance: The ECB delivered its first rate hike in nearly three years, a pivotal shift back to tightening driven by the energy supply shock from renewed Hormuz hostilities. The Bundesbank chief publicly argued the ECB should hold despite the oil surge, but was overruled. Fiscal policy across the bloc remains fragmented — defense spending pressures persist alongside austerity-leaning northern members.

New / Most Important: This ECB hike is structurally significant and breaks the easing consensus that prevailed through most of 2025-26. The central bank is now caught in a classic supply-shock trap: hiking into what was already tepid growth to contain energy-pass-through inflation. The "extremely volatile" outlook language from ECB officials signals they have low conviction in their own forward guidance. The Bundesbank dissent being made public is unusual and reveals deep internal division. The digital euro pilot moved forward with 36 payment providers selected, but this is a multi-year plumbing story, not a market mover today. The euro edged higher against GBP on the hike, but the narrowing rate gap with the BOJ is creating cross-currency complications — yen buying pressure could siphon flows from European fixed income. Rising oil prices are pushing Eurozone bond yields higher, tightening financial conditions beyond what the policy rate alone implies.

Playbook ✓: Energy shock → ECB forced to tighten → euro strengthens short-term → growth outlook deteriorates. Classic stagflationary playbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The Bundesbank publicly breaking ranks is unusual institutional signaling. If the hawks dissented against a hike, it means the ECB's reaction function is being driven more by headline oil than by underlying demand-pull inflation. This makes the hike potentially a policy error if Hormuz tensions de-escalate quickly — they'd have tightened into a growth downturn for a transient supply shock.

Macro Stance: The PBOC stays accommodative in volume but is guarding the floor on price. It boosted liquidity to smooth tax payments and debt issuance (Bloomberg, [Jul 14]), injecting 669.5 billion yuan (Crypto Briefing, [Jul 14]), yet told some banks not to re-discount bills at rates below 0.5% (Reuters, [Jul 14]). That fits its pledge to keep policy accommodative amid weak demand (Reuters, [Jul 8]) without a headline cut. The yuan fixing went below 6.8 per dollar for the first time since 2023 (Bloomberg, [Jul 10]) before UOB saw consolidation after a sharper drop (Mitrade, [Jul 13]). Prices: June CPI rose 1% (Global Times, [Jul 9]) while producer inflation hit a four-year high (Reuters, [Jul 8]), and the GDP deflator is set to turn positive (Borneo Bulletin, [Jul 14]).

PMIs & Activity: Second-quarter growth was the slowest since 2022 as investment slumped (CNBC, [Jul 14]), missed the market forecast (Reuters, [Jul 14]) and missed the growth target for the first time since Covid (CNN, [Jul 14]); first-half GDP expanded 4.7% (chinadailyhk, [Jul 14]). ING calls the slowdown worse than expected on weak domestic demand ([Jul 14]). Supply is not the problem: industrial output growth was the strongest in three months (TradingView, [Jul 14]), the June official manufacturing PMI was 50.3 (Reuters, [Jun 29]), and exports jumped 27% y/y (Reuters, [Jul 13]) to a record $412 billion (Bloomberg, [Jul 13]), lifting first-half foreign trade 16.9% (Global Times, [Jul 14]). Demand is: crude oil imports plunged to the lowest in nearly a decade (Bloomberg, [Jul 13]).

Credit Impulse: May total social financing grew 7.7% (CGTN, [Jun 12]) and topped forecasts (Bloomberg, [Jun 12]), but new loans missed as the property slump curbed demand (Reuters, [Jun 12]) and households kept deleveraging (SCMP, [Jun 15]). Government bonds carry the impulse while regulators squeeze the riskier end: up to 494.6 billion yuan of bonds face downgrade risk under the ratings crackdown (BigGo Finance, [Jul 8]) and banks were asked to avoid underwriting short-term LGFV bonds (Bloomberg, [Jul 8]). The June loan figures are still pending; an investment slump of this size suggests no private-credit revival.

Property: June new home prices fell at a slower pace, though Reuters doubts a recovery ([Jul 14]), and Bloomberg reads the easing slump as a sign the market is stabilising ([Jul 14]). The flow data are weaker: real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May (GMK Center, [Jun 18]), developers face a fresh liquidity crunch (Nikkei Asia, [Jul 13]), Vanke says its first-half loss may widen to $2.2 billion (Bloomberg, [Jul 10]), and the fiscal engine is sputtering as the land model cracks (WION, [Jul 14]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Beijing's answer is a first five-year consumption plan targeting 60 trillion yuan in retail sales by 2030 (Caixin, [Jul 14]), and Reuters expects stimulus to remain calibrated ([Jul 14]); a Caixin-cited economist wants the local-debt plan expanded ([Jul 14]). Sinocism flags preparation for the July Politburo meeting on the economy ([Jul 13]). On trade, the surplus with the EU hit a record (Bloomberg, [Jul 14]), Brussels is signalling emergency import curbs (SCMP, [Jul 14]) and warns dialogue "will not suffice" (Euronews, [Jul 14]). Washington is easier: the Russia sanctions bill cuts the tariff threat on China and India from 500% to 100% (Deccan Herald, [Jul 14]), and a tariff probe is unlikely to derail an autumn Xi-Trump meeting (SCMP, [Jul 14]).

Markets & Flows: Hong Kong fell below 24,000 on Gulf risks (VT Markets, [Jul 14]) and then rebounded on the trade data (TradingView, [Jul 14]), while the Shanghai benchmark sits near a three-month low (BBN Times, [Jul 13]). The Chinese AI stock trade has fallen about 10% on Fed jitters, though SCMP argues the structural story is intact. Bonds are pricing policy: the 10-year yield fell on stimulus bets (TradingView, [Jul 14]). Equity supply is coming, with CXMT setting a listing date for Asia's biggest IPO of 2026 (The Economic Times, [Jul 14]).

New / Most Important: The second-quarter miss is a domestic-demand miss. Output growth at a three-month high and record exports mean the factories delivered; investment and consumption did not, and the shortfall below the target range is the first since Covid. Beijing has so far answered with liquidity for tax week, a floor on bill rates and a consumption plan with a 2030 horizon, not a demand package, which leaves the July Politburo meeting as the next real decision point.

Playbook ✓: A growth miss on weak investment, export strength, a slowing but still-falling property market and calibrated support are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Markets are trading the miss as a stimulus trigger, with bond yields falling on stimulus bets; the policy signal is that support stays calibrated. If Beijing again leans on supply rather than demand, the excess output keeps flowing abroad. That is the transmission to watch. European exporters face a record bilateral surplus and a Commission now talking about emergency curbs, which raises policy risk for EU autos and machinery. Construction-linked commodities lose: an investment slump with property investment falling by double digits weighs on iron ore and AUD regardless of stronger PMIs. Oil loses a buyer as Chinese crude imports sit at a near-decade low. EM Asia benefits only through the AI-hardware export chain.

Macro Stance: The BOJ is building toward what headlines describe as its first rate hike in 31 years, with tightening "gaining momentum." Japan spent $73.7 billion defending the yen and "it's barely working." PM Takaichi's draft economic blueprint triggered a bond market rout, creating contradictory signals between fiscal expansion desires and monetary tightening.

New / Most Important: The massive pension shift toward domestic assets is the structurally transformative story here. Japan signaled a reallocation of its enormous pension pools (GPIF and related funds) toward domestic equities and bonds, which already sparked a yen and JGB rally. This is a capital flow event of the first order — Japan's pension system is one of the largest pools of capital on the planet, and any meaningful repatriation would drain liquidity from foreign bond markets (particularly US Treasuries and European sovereigns) at exactly the wrong time. The carry trade unwind fears are now colliding with easing oil prices (which should help Japan as an energy importer), creating a confusing macro signal. The Takaichi government wants fiscal expansion while the BOJ wants to tighten — this policy contradiction is rattling both bond and currency markets simultaneously. The $73.7B in yen intervention barely moving the needle tells you the structural flow forces are overwhelming the MOF's firepower. Watch for the pension repatriation to become the dominant flow story of H2 2026.

Playbook ✓: BOJ normalization → yen carry unwind → JGB volatility. Textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The pension repatriation is NOT in the consensus playbook. Most are focused on rate differentials; the pension flow channel is a structural supply/demand shift in global fixed income that could amplify Treasury yield rises far beyond what US domestic factors alone would justify.

Macro Stance: The RBA is hawkish, with a fourth rate hike now seen as increasingly likely if the US-Iran conflict persists. Westpac sees one more hike before cuts can begin. House prices and bank stocks face downside risk.

New / Most Important: The Hormuz-driven energy shock has turned Australia's rate path explicitly conditional on geopolitics — headlines framing a "fourth hike more likely if Trump's Iran conflict not resolved within a week" is an extraordinary level of geopolitical conditionality for RBA policy.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Australia as an energy exporter should benefit from higher oil — but the RBA is treating it as an inflation problem, not a terms-of-trade windfall. The disconnect between macro benefit (current account) and monetary pain (rate hikes crushing housing) could create violent sector rotation out of banks/REITs into resource names.

Macro Stance: GUS confirmed June CPI at 2.5% y/y with prices down 0.5% m/m, exactly at the NBP target and matching the flash (Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK, StockWatch.pl, Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 15]); food and fuel fell while services kept rising (Super Biznes, Radio ESKA, [Jul 15]). That is the good news. The bad news is that the market no longer believes it unlocks a cut: the end of the CPN fuel package will lift July inflation (Gazeta Prawna, Bankier.pl citing Erste, [Jul 15]), PKO BP expects a transitory rise above 3.5% that "will contribute to rate stabilisation" (PAP, [Jul 15]), pb.pl reports experts "do not believe in cuts after the holidays" as fuel prices climb again ([Jul 15]), and Parkiet says the largest bank's economists simply "do not believe Glapiński" ([Jul 15]). Add yesterday's RPP member calling a hike likelier than a cut (pb.pl, [Jul 14]) and the governor's post-holiday motion (StockWatch.pl, [Jul 9]) looks like one vote, not a majority. The reference rate remains 3.75% (PAP Biznes, [Jul 8]). Industry stalled in the latest GUS print (Forsal.pl, [Jul 13]) and the foreign trade deficit reached 12.5 billion zloty, driven by China (CEO Magazyn, [Jul 15]). Energy prices in Poland rose 15.8% on heat and geopolitics (Gramwzielone.pl, [Jul 15]), with European gas at its highest since March (Energetyka24, [Jul 15]).

Markets: Tuesday's Allegro surge carried through the card: Allegro 43.92 is +11.5% on the week and +17.0% over four weeks after preliminary results showed 3.34 billion zloty of revenue and 1.03 billion zloty of adjusted EBITDA (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 14]), and Investing.com notes WIG20 at a bull-market record with StockWatch flagging the 2007 all-time high within reach ([Jul 15]). Wednesday was more nuanced: records were set again but decliners dominated, Pepco led and Modivo and the banks were under pressure as the government "hits the banks" with its CIT proposal; sWIG80 lost 0.94% (Bankier.pl, Inwestycje.pl, FXMAG, [Jul 15]). The card shows the bank fade already: PKO 110.5 (+5.5% 1W, +4.4% 4W), Pekao 237.0 (+2.2% / +1.8%). Orlen 146.0 (+8.0% / +5.5%) is the other leader. KGHM 319.4 is flat on the week (+0.1%) but -16.9% over four weeks and gave back gains on Wednesday (XTB, [Jul 15]); PGE 9.5, Dino 28.2, CD Projekt 231.6 (-2.5% 1W) with INNPoland calling its share price "still disappointing" ([Jul 15]), LPP 19650 (+4.5% / +3.8%). EPOL 40.78 is +3.4% on the week but -0.4% over four weeks. The zloty "caught its breath": the euro stopped rising (Bankier.pl, [Jul 15]) and the zloty firmed clearly against the dollar, which returned near 3.79 (FXMAG, CEO Magazyn, [Jul 15]); the card has USD/PLN 3.7832 (+0.3% 1W, +3.7% 4W) and EUR/PLN 4.3231 (+0.5% / +2.1%). FXMAG warns that forecasts of a 7% of GDP deficit and rising debt are "hitting the zloty" ([Jul 15]).

Fiscal & Politics: The half-year budget print is the week's fiscal shock: a deficit of 123.7 billion zloty after June, with VAT receipts undermined by KSeF teething problems and cheap fuel while CIT and PIT held up (Parkiet, Rzeczpospolita, XYZ, [Jul 15]); the state spent over 402 billion zloty in H1 (Zero.pl, [Jul 15]) and debt interest now costs more than the pension subsidy (wGospodarce, [Jul 15]). This lands days after Fitch kept a negative outlook (wPolityce.pl, [Jul 13]) and the ministry's own "black scenario" warning (Strefa Biznesu, [Jul 14]). The bank CIT increase floated by Pełczyńska-Nałęcz (pb.pl, [Jul 14]) is now the policy lever the market fears most. MAN committed more than 5 billion zloty to an electric-truck plant in Małopolska (Bankier.pl, [Jul 15]). President Nawrocki has hours left to decide on the CHF-mortgage law (Franknews.pl, [Jul 15]).

Corporate & Sectors: Banks: mortgages are getting cheaper and some lenders now offer over 1.3 million zloty of capacity (Forsal.pl, Direct Money, [Jul 15]), but the CJEU will rule on the "balance theory" in CHF cases in September (Prawo.pl, Franknews.pl, [Jul 15]) and the NBP has warned of a new wave of lawsuits (Parkiet, [Jul 14]). Orlen raised wholesale fuel prices with "powerful increases" at refineries (Money.pl, Super Biznes, [Jul 15]), Azoty's Polimery Police remain idle awaiting Orlen (Parkiet, [Jul 15]), and the criminal notice against Obajtek stands (TVN24, [Jul 14]). KGHM faces a German copper programme that could threaten it (wnp.pl, [Jul 15]). Retail: UOKiK is probing Lidl and Dino for transport collusion (Wiadomości Handlowe, [Jul 15]) as a protest by dismissed Dino employees continues (ePiotrkow, [Jul 15]); the Hindenburg-related investigation into LPP was suspended (Parkiet, [Jul 15]).

Geopolitics & Security: Poland and the Baltics warned Russia could launch a limited military or hybrid provocation against NATO, and Sikorski said Moscow may stage a false-flag drone attack using Ukrainian UAVs (AP News, Kyiv Post, [Jul 15]); the FT reports Russia accused of planning attacks on Baltic or Polish infrastructure ([Jul 15]) and a Russian spy plane again tested NATO defences over the Baltic (Kyiv Post, [Jul 15]). Over 200 thousand now serve in the Polish military (Interia Biznes, [Jul 15]).

New / Most Important: The 123.7 billion zloty half-year deficit changes the policy mix. With VAT disappointing, rating outlook negative and the market now pricing cuts out rather than in, the easy "cheapest easing story in Europe" framing has lost both legs in one day: CPI at target is being overridden by the fuel-package expiry, and the fiscal side is pushing the government toward bank taxes that hit the index's largest sector. The record WIG20 is being carried by Allegro and Orlen while its traditional engine stalls.

Playbook ✓: Zloty stabilising as cut bets fade is the expected response; banks lagging on a tax threat and Allegro re-rating on earnings are both orthodox.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Inflation at 2.5% and on target while the bond and FX market trades a 7%-of-GDP deficit is a fiscal-dominance signal, not an easing signal. If the Council holds through the CPN-driven July CPI rebound and the ministry reaches for bank CIT, the equity leadership rotation away from banks will have further to run even as the headline index prints records.

Macro Stance: Investors are "suddenly fleeing Indonesia" per DW reporting. In a rising US yield environment with the dollar firming on safe-haven flows, EM capital flight is textbook — but Indonesia's speed of outflows suggests country-specific catalysts beyond the generic EM unwind.

New / Most Important: Indonesia was a consensus EM overweight through much of 2025 on the nickel/EV supply chain thesis. The sudden reversal is a cautionary tale about EM positioning when US real rates are rising and geopolitical risk premia are expanding.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: None beyond the speed of reversal.

Narrative: The Nasdaq 100 at 29,349 (↓3.9% vs 4W ago) is the worst major index, Microsoft is taking target cuts after "flaccid performance", and the AI story is splitting between infrastructure winners and the software and application layer.

Reported: IBM had its worst day on record, down 25%, after a second-quarter earnings warning (CNBC, [Jul 14]), saying the AI boom is squeezing software budgets (Reuters, [Jul 14]). Ericsson missed Q2 estimates (Investing.com, [Jul 14]) and warned over component costs (Il Sole 24 ORE, [Jul 14]). HCLTech beat on a financial-services boost (Reuters, [Jul 13]).

EPS Upside Watch: Cybersecurity — CrowdStrike got a big boost from IBM's warning (Barron's, [Jul 14]) as budgets tilt toward security. Celestica — a preview expects another beat-and-raise (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 14]), with hardware 'eating everyone's lunch' (MarketWatch, [Jul 14]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: SpaceX falling below its IPO price for the first time cracks the "private markets only go up" thesis behind late-stage venture and crossover returns. It forces mark-to-market pain on every fund that used it as a valuation anchor and puts secondary pricing for the private tech stack at risk.
Narrative: The sector is dragged by broad tech weakness but less exposed to the chip sell-off; the Batman/DCU buzz is a content-cycle catalyst for Warner Bros Discovery, not a sector-level trade.
Reported: No major reports this week; Netflix reports as the Q2 season kicks off (TradingKey, [Jul 12]).

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet — a Q2 preview sees an AWS-style blueprint for its TPUs (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 14]), a new AI revenue line. Alibaba — the shares jumped the most in ten months as earnings hopes grow (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 8]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The streaming leader sits near a 52-week low into its Q2 report (AskTraders.com, [Jul 13]), with Wall Street weighing subscriber churn and content-pipeline concerns (TradingView, [Jul 14]). Even with a World Cup ad windfall, the sector's growth may come from AI cloud, not from streaming.

Narrative: A positively sloped curve (+40 bps, little changed over four weeks) is a modest NIM tailwind, and the question is "why are big banks doing so well in this economy?"; BlackRock's Fink sees market strength and momentum.

Reported: JPMorgan posted the highest quarterly profit ever by a US bank as dealmaking and stock trading surged (Reuters, [Jul 14]). Citi beat every profit estimate (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 14]), but the shares fell on expense worries (Reuters, [Jul 14]). Bank of America rode market whiplash to trading records (Reuters, [Jul 14]), and Goldman beat with the stock up 2% (Fox Business, [Jul 14]).
EPS Upside Watch: Morgan Stanley — estimates are rising into its report (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 12]) after peers' record trading quarters.

⚡ Breaking Convention: 372 large US bankruptcies drew a muted credit response while banks post records, and Dimon calls markets 'close to as good as it gets' (Fortune, [Jul 14]). Either losses sit in private credit and CLOs, or the lag has not hit loan books yet.

Narrative: WTI at 79.56 (↓1.5% vs 4W ago) is drifting lower despite the Hormuz headlines. The growth pulse points to a supply-driven market: China's June industrial output growth was the strongest in three months and exports jumped 27%, even as its crude imports fell to the lowest in nearly a decade.

Reported: BP expects stronger Q2 earnings despite lower output (Kalkine Media, [Jul 14]) on robust oil trading, while flagging a $1 billion impairment for transition businesses (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 14]). The oil price rally added billions to Exxon's second-quarter earnings (EnergyWatch, [Jul 8]).

EPS Upside Watch: Devon Energy — earnings expectations upgraded on estimate revisions (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 10]). Cameco — a Q2 preview argues earnings could restart the nuclear rally (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 13]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oil falling while Hormuz tensions escalate means the worst is priced or reserves and rerouting work better than feared. If tensions ease, oil could drop sharply and unwind the central-bank hawkishness cascade.

Narrative: Defence is the favoured sub-sector, with Morgan Stanley putting "100% upside" on a defence name, and the AI data-centre build-out is an industrials story too: electrical equipment, cooling and construction.

Reported: Fastenal posted double-digit sales and profit increases but weaker margins (Industrial Distribution, [Jul 14]); the stock dropped, then popped (Barron's, [Jul 14]). Delta beat Q2 estimates as travel demand withstood higher prices (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 10]). DHL raised full-year guidance on an express recovery (WWD, [Jul 9]).

EPS Upside Watch: Truckers — analysts are raising truckload and LTL estimates ahead of Q2 (FreightWaves, [Jul 10]). United Airlines — expected to beat estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 8]) with ticket prices up 15-20% (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 10]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Airlines are meant to be fuel victims, yet Delta's CEO says cheaper jet fuel won't lower airfares (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 14]). If that pricing power holds, fares, not fuel, set the group's margins.
Narrative: RSM's "trickle-up economy" is the frame: asset-rich consumers keep spending, while rising rates and energy costs pressure the lower-income cohort.

Reported: Levi Strauss beat, raised guidance and lifted its dividend (CNBC, [Jul 8]). Fast Retailing raised its profit forecast while cautioning on the yen and heatwaves (Reuters, [Jul 9]), and the shares slid (NST Online, [Jul 9]). Rank Group raised profit guidance as digital growth and gaming machines boost performance (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 14]).

EPS Upside Watch: Tesla — four price-target hikes ahead of Q2 earnings (Investor's Business Daily, [Jul 14]). Marriott — raised guidance again while analysts still target just $381 (TIKR.com, [Jul 10]), leaving estimates behind the company.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Restaurants are where the squeeze shows first: Papa Murphy's will close 50 restaurants on declining sales (FOX 2, [Jul 13]) even as apparel names beat and raise. The split is by category as much as by income.

Narrative: Defensive rotation should help staples in a rising-yield, falling-Nasdaq tape, but the sector struggles when inflation expectations re-accelerate and lift input costs; Coca-Cola is flagged as a stock to buy now.

Reported: PepsiCo's Q2 sales beat estimates (TradingView, [Jul 9]), but its turnaround stutters as Americans rethink snacking (Reuters, [Jul 14]). Simply Good Foods rose as earnings and revenue topped estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 9]). China's New Hope Liuhe warned of a 1.6-1.8 billion yuan first-half loss as a pig-price slump erodes cost cuts (BigGo Finance, [Jul 14]).
EPS Upside Watch: Seven & i — the 7-Eleven owner raised guidance as gas earnings rose at its North America unit (WSJ, [Jul 9]), a fuel-margin tailwind.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples are the supposed shelter from an energy shock, yet PepsiCo says shoppers are 'worse than anticipated' on gas prices (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 9]). Volume elasticity, not just input costs, is now the risk.
Narrative: Positioning is heavy, so good news gets sold, and #FundHealthcareNotWars trending on X reflects political pressure over budget allocation between defence and healthcare.

Reported: HCA cut its 2026 earnings forecast on insurance coverage losses (Healthcare Dive, [Jul 14]), and the shares dropped as payer-mix shifts squeezed earnings (WSJ, [Jul 14]). Evotec slumped after a profit warning (Moomoo, [Jul 14]).
EPS Upside Watch: Eli Lilly — Bernstein raised its target on beat potential (Investing.com, [Jul 14]), after Guggenheim lifted its own on tirzepatide strength (Investing.com, [Jul 13]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The defensive label is cracking at the payer level: HCA's coverage losses show volume risk in a sector assumed to have none, and Q2 previews already cast healthcare as the earnings headwind (ETF Database, [Jul 13]).

Narrative: Copper at 6.34 (↓2.2%) trades as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal and is slipping with the AI and chip selling. The cyclical read comes from growth data: China's second-quarter growth was the slowest since 2022 as investment slumped, though June new home prices fell at a slower pace.

Reported: Chinese lithium miners are posting 1,000%+ profit surges as energy storage, not EVs, rescues the sector (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 14]). Covestro raised its 2026 core earnings outlook after a strong first half (Reuters, [Jul 9]). Zijin Mining's first-half profit surged 170% (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 9]).

EPS Upside Watch: Chemical producers — China's supply restraint may keep chemical prices elevated (ANI News, [Jul 13]). Gold miners — Bank of America sees value even after cutting its 2026 gold price forecast (Kitco, [Jul 13]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Gold at 4040, down 6.7% in four weeks despite the Hormuz escalation, is genuinely anomalous: Bitcoin appears to be taking gold's macro-hedge bid, and central-bank buying may be pausing after a multi-year spree.
Narrative: Rising 10Y yields (4.55, +8 bps) are kryptonite for rate-sensitive REITs, and Australian housing faces downside from further RBA hikes, a global housing-stress signal.

Reported: UK homebuilder Vistry's shares plunged on a warning of first-half losses (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 8]). China Vanke says its first-half loss may widen to $2.2 billion (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 10]). MJ Gleeson cited an uncertain outlook amid geopolitical and policy risks (Global Banking & Finance Review, [Jul 10]).
EPS Upside Watch: Schroder REIT — portfolio vacancies are at a four-year low as the Picton acquisition continues (Investment Week, [Jul 10]), supporting rental income.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Bids are rising, not falling: LondonMetric and Schroder REIT raised their offer for Picton (Property Week, [Jul 10]). Buyers see value where the rate-driven consensus sees only duration risk.

Narrative: AI data-centre power demand is the structural bull case, but rising yields (10Y at 4.55) weigh on the sector's bond-proxy valuation, and the Dow's AI data-centre play flashing a buy signal may involve utilities-adjacent names.
Reported: No major reports this week.
